Resolved up to a finite check.
Let $R_3(G)$ denote the minimal $m$ such that if the edges of $K_m$ are $3$-coloured then there must be a monochromatic copy of $G$. Show that\[R_3(C_n) \leq 4n-3.\]
#556: [Er81][Er81c]
graph theory | 
ramsey theory
A problem of Bondy and Erdős. This inequality is best possible for odd $n$. 
Luczak [Lu99] has shown that $R_3(C_n)\leq (4+o(1))n$ for all $n$, and in fact $R_3(C_n)\leq 3n+o(n)$ for even $n$.
Kohayakawa, Simonovits, and Skokan [KSS05] proved this conjecture when $n$ is sufficiently large and odd. Benevides and Skokan [BeSk09] proved that if $n$ is sufficiently large and even then $R_3(C_n)=2n$.
This problem is #25 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.

 For $n=3$, the stated inequality is false.
Indeed, $C_3=K_3$ and $R_3(C_3)=R(3,3,3)=17$ [1], whereas the proposed upper bound is $4\cdot3-3=9$. 
Hence $R_3(C_3)=17>9=4\cdot3-3.$
Thus $n=3$ is a counterexample to the statement as written: the required inequality has the opposite direction.
The intended problem is presumably for $n\ge4$. Both OEIS A389335 [1] and the current Small Ramsey Numbers survey [2] formulate the Bondy--Erdős conjecture as
$R_3(C_n)\le4n-3 \qquad (n\ge4).$
The statement on this page does, however, appear to reproduce Erdős's 1981 formulation accurately: the original source likewise gives no explicit restriction on $n$ [3]. Thus the issue does not appear to be an inaccurate transcription of Erdős's wording. Rather, an implicit restriction in the original formulation seems to need to be made explicit in the modern statement.
Could the condition $n\ge4$ (equivalently, $n>3$) be added, perhaps with a note that the unrestricted wording is inherited from the original source?
References
[1] OEIS A389335: <https://oeis.org/A389335>
[2] S. P. Radziszowski, *Small Ramsey Numbers*: <https://www.cs.rit.edu/~spr/ElJC/sur.pdf>
[3] P. Erdős, original 1981 problem formulation: <https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-32.pdf>
